entries.topic: OU Torah, "The Age to Study Kabbalah"

claims.text: Shach YD 246:6 "some have written that one should not study kabbalah until age forty"; holiness and purity; Brody 1756 endorsed by Va'ad Arba Aratzot banned Lurianic before forty, Zohar etc. over thirty, anti-Sabbatean; Emden criticised Hasidim for studying Zohar; Rav Kook 1912 practical vs intellectual; Maimonides Pardes "stomach is full with bread and meat"

claims.text: Roots in Talmud and Arab tradition on age forty; first kabbalistic restrictions Moses ben Simeon of Burgos and Abulafia school; Shem Tov ibn Gaon emphasis, traced to Solomon ibn Adret; "influential also among pupils of R. Isaac Luria"

entries.topic: My Jewish Learning, "Why Kabbalah Is Considered Dangerous"

claims.text: Four rabbis "entered pardes": one died, one went mad, one "cut off the shoots", Akiva emerged unscathed; age forty, married, versed in Torah and Talmud; danger of misinterpretation; Sabbatai Zevi as chief example, kabbalistic calculation, crisis of faith

sources.label: My Jewish Learning, "Why Kabbalah Is Considered Dangerous"

claims.text: Born 1250 León, died 1305 Arévalo; presumed author of Zohar ascribed to Simeon ben Yohai; circulating copies "since the 1280s"; wife said he was the author; Scholem: medieval, "strange, artificial, literary Aramaic", native language Hebrew; motive counter rationalism

Survived fall of Acre; went to Spain c. 1305; met de León at Valladolid; de León died before showing manuscript; wife and daughter: "Moses of Leon had written the book himself."; testimony dropped from 1580 Sefer Yuchasin, restored 1857; Scholem, Matt accept

"foundational work of Kabbalistic literature"; mainly Aramaic; publicized by de León as Shimon bar Yochai; 1280–1286; Scholem view "widely held as accurate"; Liebes and Matt; Karo accepted; Yemenite, Andalusian, some Italian communities "never accepted it as authentic"; Emden doubted; Cremona 1558, Mantua 1558–1560; draws on Sefer Yetzirah and Bahir

entries.topic: Jewish Currents, "August 4: Zohar Hot Off the Press"

claims.text: First print edition 4 Aug 1558 after a ninety-year rabbinical ban on printing the Zohar was lifted; Mantua and Cremona rival editions

sources.label: Jewish Currents, "August 4: Zohar Hot Off the Press"

claims.text: Born 1534 Jerusalem; Safed "early in 1570"; died 5 Aug 1572; "a scant two years"; Vital recorded and legitimized; tzimtzum, shevirat ha-kelim, tiqqun; "Man plays an important role in this process"; central role in Shabbetai Tzevi movement; influenced Hasidism

Born 23 July 1626 Smyrna; "steeped himself" in Kabbala; Nathan of Gaza 1665, 1666; spread to Venice, Amsterdam, Hamburg, London, North Africa; imprisoned early 1666; Sept 1666 Adrianople, threatened with torture, converted; Mehmed Efendi, doorkeeper, "a generous allowance"; died 1676

Born c. 1726 Podolia; "proclaimed himself as a direct successor to Sabbatai Zevi"; 1759 Lwów discussion presided by canon Mikulski; baptized 17 Sept 1759 and in Warsaw next day; 500+ converted in a year, nearly a thousand the next; arrested 6 Feb 1760, heresy, Częstochowa, released Aug 1772 by Bibikov; Baron of Offenbach; died 1791

entries.topic: David Assaf, "Hasidism: Historical Overview" (Tel Aviv University)

claims.text: Baal Shem Tov 1698/1700–1760, taught publicly c. 1733; literature "profoundly shaped by kabbalistic ideas"; "appealed to the masses and not only to the elite"; 1772 campaign Shklov, Vilna, Brody; Gaon of Vilna drove it; "a threat to traditional structure and order"; "quasi-Sabbatian tendencies"; "exceptionally popular in Ukraine"

sources.label: David Assaf, "Hasidism: Historical Overview" (Tel Aviv University)

claims.text: "an adherence to or communion with God that stops short of mystical union"; Deut 11:22; in Kabbalah "a privilege of the spiritual aristocracy"; in Hasidism "found expression in the social sphere", "open to every Ḥasid"

entries.topic: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, "Giovanni Pico della Mirandola"

claims.text: 900 Conclusiones printed late 1486 in Rome; "the claim that magic and Kabbalah proved Christ's divinity"; Flavius Mithridates translated, inserted Christian wording; Innocent VIII indicted 13, denounced whole; Pico fled to France, arrested at pope's request

sources.label: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, "Giovanni Pico della Mirandola"

claims.text: "a dogmatic weapon to turn back against the Jews to compel their conversion"; Reuchlin "Pico's most important follower"; De arte cabalistica; Kircher Tree of Life used in Hermetic Qabalah

1455–1522; De arte Cabalistica 1517 Haguenau; 1510 Pfefferkorn; Talmud "was not composed for every blackguard to trample with unwashed feet"; Augenspiegel 1511; Leo X decided against him 1520; works placed on the Index
